title: The Marathon Majors: Why 26.2 Miles Remains Sport's Most Brutal and Beautiful Challenge
summary: Boston, Tokyo, London, Berlin, Chicago, New York. The six Marathon Majors represent the pinnacle of long-distance running. We look at what makes them special — and the athletes pushing the boundaries of what is humanly possible.
content:
There is something primal about the marathon. Twenty-six point two miles on foot, against the clock, against the course, against yourself. No team-mates to carry you. No substitutions when the legs go. Just you and the road and the question of how deep you are willing to dig.

The six World Marathon Majors — Tokyo, Boston, London, Berlin, Chicago, New York — represent the pinnacle of the sport. Each has its own character, its own course, its own relationship with the city that hosts it. Together they form a calendar that elite marathon runners plan their entire year around.

Berlin — Where Records Fall

If you want to run the fastest marathon of your life, you go to Berlin. The course is flat, the autumn conditions are ideal, and the organisation is immaculate. More world records have been set in Berlin than at any other marathon in history. Eliud Kipchoge chose Berlin to run his sub-two-hour time trial for a reason.

The current men's world record — set on these streets — represents a pace that would have seemed science fiction to runners a generation ago. The women's record is similarly extraordinary. Berlin has become the laboratory where the limits of human endurance are most rigorously tested.

London — The People's Race

The London Marathon is unique among the Majors in the way it blurs the line between elite sport and mass participation. The world's best runners compete at the front while tens of thousands of ordinary people — some in elaborate costumes, some raising money for charity, all pushing their own limits — complete the same course on the same day.

Running the London Marathon is one of the great shared experiences in British sport. The crowd carries you in ways you cannot predict and cannot prepare for.

New York and Boston — Prestige Above All

Boston's qualifying standard makes it the marathon that serious recreational runners spend years working toward. The Heartbreak Hill finish, the passionate crowds, the history — it carries a weight that the other Majors cannot quite replicate. Winning Boston means something specific in the running world.

New York, meanwhile, is the spectacle — five boroughs, two million spectators, a finish in Central Park that has provided some of the sport's most iconic images. The course is not fast. It doesn't matter. Nobody goes to New York just for a personal best.

The New Generation of Marathoners

What is most exciting about marathon running right now is the depth of talent. Kipchoge's era of near-total dominance in the men's race is being challenged by a wave of East African runners who have trained specifically to beat him. The women's field has never been deeper or faster.

The world record will fall again. It is simply a question of when, and in which city.
